feature: Platform spike: subagent model inheritance and eval fidelity
problem: Both library/cursor/agents/planner.md and evaluator.md have model: inherit. Before designing per-role model routing, we need empirical understanding of: (1) how Cursor honors the model: frontmatter field on subagent Task invocations, (2) what conditions cause Cursor to override configured models, and (3) whether eval scenarios can meaningfully test role-specific model routing or only proxy builder-model behavior. Without this, feat-role-model-config risks promising what the platform cannot deliver.
proposed_solution: Research deliverable only — no implementation changes. Produce .harness/docs/research/model-selection.md with a Platform Mechanics section covering: what model: inherit means in practice, when Cursor overrides configured models (plan/admin/Max Mode conditions), what changing from inherit to a specific model ID would actually do to planner and evaluator subagents, and what eval sandbox can and cannot observe. Source: Cursor subagent platform docs + reasoning from existing Phase 5 multi-agent research.
acceptance_criteria: model-selection.md exists at .harness/docs/research/model-selection.md and contains a 'Platform Mechanics' section that answers the research question: test $(grep -c '## Platform Mechanics' .harness/docs/research/model-selection.md) -ge 1 && echo PASS-AC1

Platform Mechanics section explicitly documents the three conditions under which Cursor overrides configured model: (team admin restrictions, Max Mode required, plan limitations): python3 -c "content=open('.harness/docs/research/model-selection.md').read(); assert 'admin' in content.lower() and 'max mode' in content.lower() and 'plan' in content.lower(), 'Missing override conditions'" && echo PASS-AC2

Document includes explicit scope boundary for feat-eval-role-model-matrix: what eval CAN observe vs what is BLOCKED by platform constraints. Must contain a 'Eval Fidelity' or 'What eval can observe' subsection: test $(grep -ci 'eval.*fidelity\|what eval\|eval can\|blocked' .harness/docs/research/model-selection.md) -ge 1 && echo PASS-AC3

Document includes concrete recommendation for feat-role-model-config: which model field values to use for planner and evaluator (not 'TBD'), with rationale. Must reference specific model IDs or tiers: python3 -c "content=open('.harness/docs/research/model-selection.md').read(); assert 'planner' in content and 'evaluator' in content and ('composer' in content.lower() or 'model id' in content.lower() or 'fast' in content.lower() or 'inherit' in content.lower())" && echo PASS-AC4

state.json marks spike-subagent-model-mechanics status as 'building': python3 -c "import json; s=json.load(open('.harness/state.json')); task=next(t for t in s['tasks'] if t['id']=='spike-subagent-model-mechanics'); assert task['status']=='building', f'status={task[\"status\"]}'" && echo PASS-AC5
edge_cases: Platform docs may have changed since Phase 5 research — cross-reference Phase 5 (phase-5-multi-agent.md) findings on context isolation with new subagent docs; flag any contradictions explicitly
Model IDs evolve: document should list currently valid IDs from SDK skill (composer-2.5, auto) without hard-coding assumptions about future availability

Eval sandbox uses Agent.prompt() or session_runner.py which sets model= explicitly — this is different from IDE Task tool invocation which reads frontmatter; distinguish both paths in the eval fidelity section
verification_method:
Run from repo root:

test $(grep -c '## Platform Mechanics' .harness/docs/research/model-selection.md) -ge 1 && echo PASS-AC1
# AC2: three override conditions documented
python3 -c "content=open('.harness/docs/research/model-selection.md').read(); assert 'admin' in content.lower() and 'max mode' in content.lower() and 'plan' in content.lower(); print('PASS-AC2')"
# AC3: eval fidelity scope boundary
test $(grep -ci 'eval.*fidelity\|what eval\|eval can\|blocked' .harness/docs/research/model-selection.md) -ge 1 && echo PASS-AC3
# AC4: concrete model recommendation
python3 -c "content=open('.harness/docs/research/model-selection.md').read(); assert 'planner' in content and 'evaluator' in content; print('PASS-AC4')"
# AC5: task status = building
python3 -c "import json; s=json.load(open('.harness/state.json')); task=next(t for t in s['tasks'] if t['id']=='spike-subagent-model-mechanics'); assert task['status']=='building'; print('PASS-AC5')"
